scenes.title: 1974 Stirling / Cambridge Dual-Task Bench: Chanting 8 Digits Aloud ('6-1-9-4-8-2-7-3') While Solving 'BA' Logic Cards at 95% Accuracy!
scenes.era: 1974, University of Stirling / MRC Cambridge Psychology Lab

layout.description: Sunlit high-key 1974 British cognitive psychology room featuring a clean oak desk holding **8-Digit Memory Load Cards ('6 — 1 — 9 — 4 — 8 — 2 — 7 — 3')**, crisp **Grammatical Reasoning Flashcards ('A is NOT preceded by B -> [ B A ] True or False?')**, a two-button response timer showing **95% Accuracy (2.15s -> 3.27s)**, and Baddeley & Hitch's **4-Box Working Memory Blueprint** on the wall easel.

positions.who: Alan Baddeley & Graham Hitch (mannequins in 1974 British corduroy/tweed blazers and ties)
positions.where: flipping the 'B A' grammatical reasoning card and staring impressed at the flat 95%-accuracy line even at an 8-digit vocal load
rhythmically reciting '6-1-9-4-8-2-7-3' aloud while simultaneously tapping the 'TRUE' button accurately for 'A is not preceded by B -> BA'!

props.name: 8-Digit Vocal Load Strip & 'A is NOT preceded by B -> [B A]' Logic Card
props.period_detail: pits full verbal rehearsal directly against active reasoning
props.physical_behavior: Baddeley & Hitch's exact 1974 experiment that toppled unitary STM

props.name: Accuracy & Latency Graph ('0 Digits: 2.15s / 95% -> 8 Digits: 3.27s / 95% — No Crash!')
props.period_detail: shows smooth graceful trade-off instead of the predicted 50% collapse
props.physical_behavior: empirical proof of separate working-memory components

props.name: 4-Room Working Memory Blueprint (Central Executive -> Phonological Loop | Visuospatial Sketchpad | Episodic Buffer)
props.period_detail: clean architectural schematic beside the table

actions.verb_sequence: keeps reciting the 8-digit string aloud without dropping a digit -> inspects '[B A]' logic card -> presses 'TRUE' cleanly in 3.2 seconds
points from the 95% accuracy line to the separated Central Executive and Phonological Loop rooms on the easel

reactions.reaction: exchange an excited look realizing 'Short-Term Memory' is a multi-part active workshop
completes the block with 95% reasoning accuracy intact

scenes.wardrobe: 1974 British university attire: tan corduroy/tweed jackets, patterned ties, collared shirts, V-neck wool jumper.
scenes.recognition_hook: Stuff their verbal short-term memory to the absolute brim with 8 random digits — and watch them still nail tricky logic puzzles at 95% accuracy!

key_visual.description: a 1974 psychology desk with an 8-digit card, a 'B A' grammatical logic card, and a 95%-accuracy timer alongside a 4-box Working Memory diagram as a seated subject chants digits while tapping True
